newsitem.title: USA: Prudential Insurance confirms reaches settlement.
newsitem.headline: Prudential Insurance confirms reaches settlement.

text.p: Prudential Insurance Co of America said Tuesday it has settled a class-action lawsuit brought against it by life insurance policyholders for a minimum of $410 million in remedies.
The lawsuit alleged that Prudential misled policyholders to get them to buy pricier insurance policies.
The settlement applies to the owners of more than 10 million Prudential permanent life insurance policies purchased between 1982 and 1995.

Prudential may provide other guaranteed values depending on the number of remediated claims under the alternative-dispute resolution process. The total cost of that process is not capped and will depend on the actual number of claims remedied, the company said.
Forty-three states and the District of Columbia previously agreed to the program established to provide remediation and are reviewing the terms of the settlement.

Seven other states, including California, Texas, Massachusetts and Florida, have opposed the settlement because of concerns that it would hurt their efforts to negotiate better terms for policyholders in their states, according to a report last week in the Wall Street Journal.
